clue.text: Such a remarkable piece in Sultan's collection

indicators.note: a piece in the words that follow means a stretch of their letters is lifted out whole

explanation.surface: A remarkable item forms part of a sultan's treasured collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such a remarkable piece' reads as an object in a collection, but 'piece in' asks for letters taken from inside 'Such a remarkable'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultan's household of wives and concubines was traditionally kept together in secluded quarters, a collection of women.

parts.note: a man's thing is his, the possessive pronoun
terror is sudden panic

explanation.surface: Some Spanish man is gripped by fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Hispanic describes things relating to Spain or Spanish-speaking peoples, a near synonym.

clue.text: He's pragmatic, putting the genuine first

parts.note: genuine means real
first is written 1st, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A practical man always puts what is authentic before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting the genuine first' reads as a description of the man, but it is a recipe: REAL, then 1ST spelt with I for the figure one.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with a practical, down-to-earth outlook who deals with things as they are.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clever ploy was devised as a means of defence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constructed has been built or put together, i.e. produced.

clue.text: A strong father deflects tons of insults

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical marking for loud or strong
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: to deflect is to turn something aside, so the letters of the word tons are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A powerful dad turns aside a great many slights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deflects' turns TONS into ONTS, which follows A, F and FR.
explanation.definitionFit: An affront is a deliberate slight or offence, so the plural matches insults as a noun.

clue.text: Fat man insulted badly by dogmatist

indicators.note: badly suggests the words are mangled, so the letters of fat man insulted are rearranged

explanation.surface: An overweight man is cruelly abused by a narrow-minded zealot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges the fourteen letters of 'Fat man insulted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who insists rigidly on the literal truth of a doctrine is a dogmatic person.

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the farewell inscribed on gravestones
in bridge the four hands are North, South, East and West, so E (East) is a hand

explanation.surface: A farewell note is lying close by, prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hand' looks like 'nearby', but 'hand' is the bridge player East, E, placed after RIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is ripe is fully developed and fit to eat, so prepared or matured.

indicators.note: told means spoken out, so the phrase is heard rather than written

parts.note: wicked means naughty and a story is a lie, giving the phrase naughty lie

explanation.surface: Someone recounts an evil tale about seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'told' signals that 'naughty lie' (wicked story) is spoken, giving the plural of a spiral-shelled sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The nautilus is a cephalopod mollusc with a chambered coiled shell, loosely grouped as shellfish.

clue.text: Woman will shortly be a hard case

parts.note: a woman is referred to as she
will shortened is the contraction 'll

explanation.surface: A woman will soon prove to be a tough nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hard case' sounds like a tough person but is literal: a rigid outer covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell is the rigid protective outer covering of an egg, nut or creature.

clue.text: Counterpart comes to very different figure

parts.note: things that are very different are opposite
a figure is a number

explanation.surface: An equivalent turns out to be a wholly unlike digit.
explanation.definitionFit: Your equivalent in another team or organisation, holding the matching role, is your counterpart.

explanation.surface: A story may be believable, but it forgets the appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim that stands up holds good under scrutiny; to stand someone up is to fail to turn up for a romantic meeting.

clue.text: The main god of the Romans

definitions.text: The main god of the Romans

parts.words: The main god of the Romans
parts.note: the main is the sea, so this is the Roman deity of the ocean, not their chief god

explanation.surface: Who ruled as chief deity in ancient Rome?
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like 'chief' (Jupiter), but it is the old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman sea deity, counterpart of the Greek Poseidon, ruled over the oceans.

parts.note: the tit is a small common songbird

explanation.surface: A small bird is bustling about.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at it is an idiom for being hard at work on something, i.e. occupied.

parts.note: ay or aye is an old poetic word meaning always

explanation.surface: Something forever carrying out an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A foray is a sudden raid or attack into enemy territory.

explanation.surface: A question about the playwright's resolve, or his last testament.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's first name was William, so he is WILL; the phrase also hints at his famous will.
explanation.definitionFit: Will is a short form of William, the playwright's first name; it also means resolve or firm intent.

clue.text: Quench flames at last with water

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word flames

parts.note: a lake is a body of water

explanation.surface: Finally put out a fire with water.
explanation.definitionFit: To slake a thirst or fire is to satisfy or extinguish it.

explanation.surface: A rigid book binding.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means severe or strict; the stern of a ship is its rear part.

indicators.note: ruined says the words are wrecked, so the letters of senile litigant are rearranged

explanation.surface: Brainy people have destroyed an old man who keeps suing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges the fourteen letters of 'senile litigant'.
explanation.definitionFit: The intellectual elite of a society, its thinkers and scholars, as a collective noun.

explanation.surface: A woman named after carefulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudence is a female first name; it also means careful good judgement.

clue.text: The chap behind, with superior road skills?

definitions.text: The chap behind, with superior road skills?

parts.words: The chap behind, with superior road skills?
parts.note: a passenger in the rear of a car who thinks he drives better and keeps telling the driver what to do

explanation.surface: Praise for the man following in traffic, an expert motorist?
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior' is ironic: this passenger only believes his skills are better.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear-seat passenger who gives unwanted directions to the person at the wheel, or any meddler.

explanation.surface: Weigh up a deal made with the lender.
explanation.definitionFit: To account something so is to regard it so; a bank account is a customer's arrangement with the bank.

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
zero looks like the letter O
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A six-nil scoreline, rapid and angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like 'quick' but is the religious fast, LENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent conduct is fierce and raging, with great force or passion.

explanation.surface: Loot and set ablaze.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to pillage it; to sack an employee is to dismiss them.

explanation.surface: A brawl over a tiny portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a minor scuffle; a scrap is also a small fragment.

clue.text: Solid money to be found in Northern town

indicators.note: to be found in places the money inside the town, as if located within it

parts.note: Bury is a town near Manchester in the north of England
L stands for pound (libra), the British currency unit

explanation.surface: Reliable funds are located in a town in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be found in' puts L inside BURY, a town in Greater Manchester, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A burly person is sturdily built and strong, heavily solid.

explanation.surface: Stoop above the enclosure for the flock.
explanation.definitionFit: To fold something is to bend one part over another; a fold is an enclosure for sheep.

explanation.surface: Rise and have a scrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The wash of a boat is the disturbed water behind it; to wash is to bathe.

explanation.surface: Meals for a caterpillar.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is slang for food; a grub is the soft larva of an insect.

clue.text: Fruity term employed by improvising actor

definitions.text: Fruity term employed by improvising actor

parts.words: Fruity term employed by improvising actor
parts.note: a plant eaten as fruit whose name extras mutter repeatedly to imitate background chatter in crowd scenes

explanation.surface: A rich expression used by a performer making up lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruity' suggests a rude word, but it means named after a fruit-like plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The pink-stalked plant cooked as a fruit, and stage chatter or nonsense talk.

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters lose their order, so the words nurse go are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medic drives a nurse out of her mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the anagram verb, but it is the definition; 'mad' rearranges 'nurse go'.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a medical practitioner who operates, a kind of medic.

indicators.note: resulting suggests what comes out when the words drops the are broken up, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone lets fall an ancient pot, and here is the fragment that results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resulting' rearranges 'Drops the'; the whole clue also describes how a broken pot leaves this.
explanation.definitionFit: A potsherd is a broken fragment of pottery, typically found by archaeologists.

parts.note: a bat is a stick used to hit a ball

explanation.surface: A man with a club heads off for a scrub.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to immerse oneself in water to clean the body.
